steps.message: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: We are building Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, as a Rust web application. Start in the `/app` Git repository: it has a minimal Cargo project (`quizzy`) and no app yet. Rust (stable), Cargo, SQLite (the library and the CLI), and Chromium are installed. You can download crates from crates.io; other network access is blocked. Fetch and build all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the build, the database, and so on) and runs the app in release mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`. It must work offline (for example, `cargo build --release --offline`), and it should start in a few minutes at most.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

The game works, and now we want prizes.

The quiz settings get a new field, "Number of winners" (a number, at least 1, 3 by default).

Scoring:

- Each correct answer gives one point.
- Players with equal points are ranked by speed: the total time of their correct answers wins when it is lower. The time of an answer runs from the moment the question opens to the player's last pick.
- Players don't see points during the game.

Speed now decides ties, so all players must get each question at the same moment: the big screen and the phones must follow the moderator close to instantly.

After "End quiz":

- The big screen shows the leaderboard: one list item for each player, in order, with the place, the name, and the points ("2 points", "1 point", "0 points").
- Each player's phone shows the place ("Place 2 of 5") and the points ("3 points").

Picking the winners (N is the number of winners):

- The "Top N" button (for example, "Top 3") makes the first N players of the leaderboard the winners.
- The "Draw" button is for ties. Every player with more points than the N-th place wins. The remaining prizes are drawn at random among the players with exactly the N-th place's points (speed doesn't matter here). Each click draws again.
- Players with 0 points never win. If fewer than N players have points, all of them win.
- The "Reset winners" button removes the winners.
- Winners get the "Winner" mark on the leaderboard, and their phones show "You won!". Both update live.

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "# Quizzy: design notes

## Stack
- Rust 2024, axum 0.8 + tokio, rusqlite with `bundled` SQLite (no system lib needed).
- Server-rendered HTML built with `format!` in `src/views.rs`. Every user string goes through `views::esc`
  (and through `js_attr` when it ends up inside an inline `confirm('…')`).
- Assets: `static/quizzy.css` (the design stylesheet plus a small "App additions" block at the end) and
  `static/Inter-latin.woff2`. Both are compiled into the binary (`include_str!`/`include_bytes!`) and served at `/assets/…`.

## Running
- `bin/serve`: `cargo build --release --offline --locked`, then exec `target/release/quizzy`.
  Env: `PORT` (default 3000), `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE` (unused so far),
  `QUIZZY_STORAGE` (default `storage`). It listens on 0.0.0.0 and accepts any Host. `GET /up` returns 200.
- Data: `storage/quizzy.sqlite3` (WAL). The schema is migrated on boot with `PRAGMA user_version`
  (`db::migrate`). **To change the schema, append a new step to the list. Never edit an old step.**

## Layout of the code
- `src/main.rs`: routes, handlers, form parsing/validation, preview logic.
- `src/auth.rs`: Basic auth middleware. It's applied app-wide and guards every path under `/moderate`
  (unknown ones too), returning 401 + `WWW-Authenticate`.
- `src/db.rs`: all SQL. Tables: `quizzes`, `questions` (position, active), `options` (position, correct).
  FKs use `ON DELETE CASCADE` (`PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON`).
- `src/views.rs`: pages.
- `src/transfer.rs`: quiz export/import JSON (serde_json with `preserve_order`), validation of imports.
- `src/game.rs`: live game handlers (big screen, player pages, SSE streams). `src/game_views.rs`: their HTML.
- `src/live.rs`: in-memory hub per game: `watch` channels (`phase`, `stats`) + player presence.

## Routes (all under /moderate need auth)
- `GET /moderate`: quiz list (`ul.quiz-list > li`)
- `GET /moderate/quizzes/new`, `POST /moderate/quizzes`
- `GET /moderate/quizzes/{id}`: quiz page (`ol.question-list > li.question-item`)
- `GET /moderate/quizzes/{id}/edit` ("Settings"), `POST /moderate/quizzes/{id}`, `POST …/delete`
- `GET …/questions/new`, `POST …/questions`, `GET …/questions/{qid}/edit`, `POST …/questions/{qid}`
- `POST …/questions/{qid}/move` (direction=up|down), `…/active`, `…/delete`
- `GET …/export` ("Export": the JSON in the page's only `<pre>`), `GET …/export.json` (download)
- `GET /moderate/quizzes/import` ("Import quiz"), `POST /moderate/quizzes/import` (field `json`, label "Quiz JSON")
- `GET …/preview?step=N&score=S&pick=OPTION_ID` / `?done=1&score=S`: stateless, the URL holds all state, nothing is stored.

## Behaviour details
- Question form fields: `body`, `active` (hidden `0` + checkbox `1`), `option_N_text`, `option_N_correct`,
  `option_N_id` (existing options). On edit, existing options are updated in place (their ids stay stable, which
  matters for future answers). Removed rows are deleted. The form always shows at least 4 rows.
- "Add option" is a submit button (`name=add_option`). JS intercepts it and appends a row from a `<template>`,
  then renumbers labels. Without JS the server re-renders with one more row.
- Labels: text inputs have a visually hidden `<label>` "Option N" + placeholder "Option N"; checkboxes have
  `aria-label="Option N is correct"` (the visible text is "Correct").
- The quiz page's "Active" checkbox saves via `fetch(…, {keepalive: true})` (204 response when `X-Requested-With`
  is set). Then the JS renumbers active questions client-side. It has a `<noscript>` fallback.
- Inactive questions are dimmed and numbered "—" on the quiz page. The preview skips them.
- Validation errors re-render the form with 422 and keep the input.
  Messages: "Add at least two options", "Mark at least one option as correct", "Question can't be blank", "Title can't be blank".
- Confirmations: `onsubmit="return confirm(…)"` on the delete forms.

## Export / import
- Format: `{"title", "questions": [{"text", "active", "options": [{"text", "correct"}]}]}`. Export writes exactly
  these keys in this order (serde structs) and always writes `active`/`correct`. Nothing else (no ids, no dates).
- Import: `active` defaults to true, `correct` to false; null counts as missing; unknown keys are ignored;
  a missing `questions` means an empty quiz. Strings are trimmed. Wrong types are errors.
- Rules are the same as the forms: title not blank (≤200 chars), question not blank (≤1000), ≥2 options, ≥1 correct,
  option text ≤500. Blank option text is an error (no silent drops on import). Errors are prefixed
  "Question N:" / "Question N, option M:", and the form is shown again with 422 and the pasted text kept.
- Validation runs fully before any write; the insert (`db::import_quiz`) is one transaction. It always creates a new quiz.

## Live game (games, players, answers)
- Schema step 2: `games` (code UNIQUE, `state` lobby|open|closed|over, `question_id`, `question_num`, `seq`),
  `game_questions` (played questions, `num`, opened/closed timestamps), `players` (`token` UNIQUE, name),
  `answers` (PK `(player_id, question_id)`, `option_id`, client `seq`, ms timestamp).
- Routes: `POST /moderate/quizzes/{id}/games` ("Start a game") → `GET /moderate/games/{id}` (big screen),
  `GET …/events` (SSE), `POST …/{start|finish|next|end}` (field `seq`). Players: `GET /play/{CODE}`,
  `POST /play/{CODE}/join` (`name`), `…/answer` (`question`, `option`, `seq`), `…/leave` (beacon, `cid`), `GET …/events?cid=`.
- Order: the next question is the first *active* question (quiz order) not yet played in this game. "Question N of M":
  N = `question_num`, M = N + remaining active unplayed. "End quiz" replaces "Next" when nothing remains.
  Starting with no active questions ends the game at once.
- Every moderator action carries the game's `seq`; a mismatch (double click, stale tab) is a no-op.
- Player identity: random token in cookie `quizzy_player_{CODE}` (Path=/play/{CODE}, HttpOnly, 30 days).
  Codes are 5 chars without 0/O/1/I/L; lowercase URLs redirect to uppercase (cookie paths are case-sensitive).
- Correct answers are never rendered on the phone until the question is closed (the open view has no
  `is-correct`, no "Correct"). The big screen also only marks "Correct" after "Finish".
- Answers: the last tap wins. JS sends `seq = max(Date.now(), last+1)`; the upsert ignores lower seqs (late retries).
  No-JS form posts use the server clock. Answers are accepted only while that question is open and the option belongs to it.
- Live updates: SSE (`EventSource`, auto-reconnect, `retry: 1500`, keep-alive comments every 2s). Each event is the full
  rendered state (not a diff), so a reconnect or a missed event self-heals. Clients drop events with an older `seq`.
  - Big screen: event `screen` (`{seq, body, controls, stats}`) on phase changes, `stats` (`{players, answered, in_game}`)
    on counter changes (coalesced 100ms). Its buttons submit via fetch and apply the JSON response directly.
  - Phone: event `view` (`{seq, html}`), re-rendered per player only on phase changes. Taps are optimistic
    ("Your answer" at once), POSTed with retries; the response is the fresh fragment.
  - Event `gone` (game deleted) makes the client reload.
- Presence ("Players: N" / the second number in "Answers: a / b"): a player counts while they have an open SSE
  connection, or within `live::GRACE` (2.5s) after it dropped or after a page load. `pagehide` sends a beacon to
  `/leave` which drops them immediately. "In the game" = present ∪ answered the current question.
- Graceful shutdown flips `hub.shutdown`, which ends all SSE streams (otherwise axum would wait forever).
- Big screen avoids duplicate visible text (title only in the lobby h1, join link only once per view) so text-based
  locators stay unique.

## Testing
- `docs/e2e/cdp.py` is a tiny stdlib-only Chrome DevTools client (no Playwright available offline).
  `docs/e2e/test.py` runs a full browser scenario against a server running on :3000 with mod:secret:
  `python3 docs/e2e/test.py`.
- `docs/e2e/game_test.py`: live game with a moderator and several players, each in its own browser context
  (`Target.createBrowserContext`), on a separate debugging port (9334).

export PORT="${PORT:-3000}"

if ! cargo build --release --offline --locked; then

  cargo build --release --offline
fi

# The database schema is created/migrated by the app on boot (storage/quizzy.sqlite3).
exec ./target/release/quizzy

I should limit the 100ms sleep to stats changes only, not phase changes, since phone streams re-render fine on their own. Connection limits aren't an issue since the big screen uses a single SSE connection, and question timing measured from server open seems fine too. I'm also noting that the phone's closed phase showing "Correct!"/"Wrong!" doesn't count as revealing points during the game.

For the over phase, I should replace "Score: x/y" with something like "Place 2 of 5" and "3 points." Late-joining players after the over phase just see the over page, which is fine.

For the leaderboard, I need to include every player in the game even those with zero points, ranked by points descending then total time ascending for correct answers, with ties broken deterministically by join order. I'll use sequential unique positions (1..n) rather than shared/competition ranking to keep things simple, which aligns with how "Top N" winner rules should work — the first N players in that ordering are declared winners.

For the "Top N" rule, if fewer than N players have points greater than zero, all of them win; otherwise it's the top N by position. For "Draw" mode, I'll find the points value of the N-th ranked player — anyone with more points automatically wins, and I randomly sample from those tied at that exact point value to fill the remaining winner slots, naturally falling back to "all players with points win" when fewer than N have any points at all.

I'm setting up a `game_winners` table keyed by game and player, then bumping the sequence and phase afterward. The over-phase screen needs a leaderboard with winner indicators and buttons for "Top 3," "Draw," "Reset winners," and "Back to quiz."

On the player's view I want text like "Place 2 of 5," "3 points," and "You won!" for winners, with singular/plural point formatting handled correctly. I'm structuring each leaderboard row with distinct place, name, and points elements so QA checks can verify a player's name, points, and winner status appear correctly in order.

Since flex-item spacing can get weird with innerText, I need to make sure there are real spaces between the text spans rather than relying on CSS layout to add them. I also want to avoid the heading "Winners" since it would accidentally match substring searches for "Winner," and I should be careful that button labels like "Reset winners" don't cause unintended matches given Playwright's case-insensitive text search.

Now I'm weighing where "number of winners" belongs—likely on settings (and maybe the new quiz form too), with validation requiring at least 1 winner and a default of 3. For export/import, I'm leaning toward leaving the format untouched to avoid breaking existing key-exactness tests, even though that means the setting won't round-trip through export.

The Over phase should keep its existing "The quiz is over" heading on both screen and phone views, with the leaderboard and placement info added underneath—making the screen version scrollable for long player lists. Scoring needs to include players who never answered at zero points, and time is computed as the sum of answered_at minus opened_at across correct answers only, using server-side timestamps so no-JS submissions behave consistently.

Prizes now work end to end: scoring with speed as the tie-breaker, the leaderboard after "End quiz", the results on each phone, and "Top N", "Draw" and "Reset winners" updating live. All three browser test suites pass with no failures (the two existing ones and a new prizes one), the new unit tests pass, and the offline `--locked` release build succeeds. No new crates were needed.

I also found what was slowing the big screen down: every live update waited an extra 100 ms, including the moderator's own moves. Now only bursts of answer-counter updates are batched, and a new question or phase goes out at once. In the test the question reached all five phones within one 0.1-second check.

The live game existed in the repo as uncommitted work; I built on top of it and haven't committed anything.

- **Settings:** "Number of winners" is on both the new-quiz and Settings forms: a number, at least 1, 3 by default. Invalid values re-show the form with an error. The value is read when a button is clicked, so changing it after the game updates the "Top N" button (I used this in the test).
- **Scoring:** one point per correct answer. Equal points are ranked by the total time of correct answers, from the question opening (server time) to the player's last pick. If that's equal too (for example, everyone on 0 points), join order decides, so every player gets a unique place. Players see no points until the end.
- **After "End quiz":** the big screen lists every player in order with place, name and points ("2 points", "1 point", "0 points"). Each phone shows "Place 2 of 5" and "3 points". The answer times appear only as a tooltip on each leaderboard row.
- **Winners:**
  - "Top N" picks the first N players. "Draw" picks at random among those tied on the N-th place's points, and each click draws again; the test saw both tied players drawn.
  - Players with 0 points never win, and if fewer than N have points, all of them win.
  - Winners get a "Winner" mark on the leaderboard and "You won!" on their phone. Both update live and survive a page reload.
  - These buttons only work after the game has ended.
- **Database:** the change is a new migration step, so existing databases upgrade on boot. I checked this against your current `storage/` data.

**Decision for you:** quiz export and import don't include the number of winners. The documented format is a fixed list of fields, so I left it alone, which means an imported quiz always starts at 3. Adding it is easy if you want it to carry over.

The core change is in `src/db.rs` and `src/game.rs`, with the winner rules in a new `src/prizes.rs`. The new test is `docs/e2e/prizes_test.py`, and I added a "Prizes" section to `docs/NOTES.md`.
